Delineation

dih-lin-ee-AY-shun · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Delineation is a precise description or representation of something.

The property survey gave a precise delineation of the boundary, down to the exact bend in the creek.

Worked Example

The zoning map offered a clear delineation of exactly where the residential district ended and the commercial one began.

The map didn't leave any fuzzy edges -- it marked the exact line, which is exactly what makes it a delineation rather than a rough sketch.

How Delineation Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

outline

outline: a description of the main shape or features of something

specification

specification: a precise, detailed statement of requirements

Antonyms

vagueness

vagueness: a lack of clear detail or definition

How Strong Is It? — description → delineation → blueprint

description vs. delineation

description vs. delineation: A description can be loose or general; a delineation is specifically precise, often with exact boundaries or details.

blueprint vs. delineation

blueprint vs. delineation: A blueprint goes even further than a delineation, providing a complete, exact technical plan rather than just a precise outline.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — de-

prefix — de-: down/completely (Latin)

root — line

root — line: line (Latin (linea))

suffix — -ation

suffix — -ation: act or process of (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: De- ('down/completely') plus line (from Latin linea) plus -ation ('act or process of') gives 'the act of marking out with a line' -- a delineation traces the exact outline or boundary of something.

Use the root in a new word: linear

Use the root in a new word: linear: Linear comes from the very same 'line' root -- describing anything arranged in or related to a straight line.
